proof_obligations.statement: Derive every carry ANF coefficient from Lucas' theorem and the Boolean generating-function factorization.
Determine whether dense invertible affine preprocessing can reduce the selected carry to bounded degree.
Construct or obstruct a polynomial-size low-degree lift using carry or arithmetic auxiliary variables.
Prove or refute exponential approximate Schmidt rank for all dense GL(m,2) splits; high ANF degree is insufficient.

summary: Upgraded finite carry-degree evidence to an exact symbolic theorem: a random density-one instance has an Omega(m)-degree carry with exponentially many top ANF monomials, invariant under every dense invertible affine reparameterization.

theorem.affine_invariance: deg(f composed with L)=deg(f) for every invertible affine L, by applying the degree upper bound to L and L inverse
theorem.anf_coefficient_formula: hat f(I)=[z^(2^j)] product_(i in I)((1+z)^a_i-1) over F_2
theorem.exact_degree_condition: if O labels are odd and O>=2^j, degree(f_j)=2^j and at least binom(O,2^j) top-degree monomials occur
theorem.lucas_bit_identity: bit_j(s)=binom(s,2^j) mod 2 for every nonnegative integer s
theorem.obstruction_scope: bounded-degree ANF reconstruction after arbitrary dense affine Boolean preprocessing, without auxiliary variables
theorem.random_label_consequence: for 2^j in (m/12,m/6], degree Theta(m) with exp(Omega(m)) top monomials except with probability exp(-m/36)

theorem_contract.conclusion: with failure exp(-Omega(m)), some carry predicate retains degree Omega(m) and exponential ANF top support
theorem_contract.non_claim: no lower bound for auxiliary-variable systems, arithmetic circuits, tensor networks, quantum circuits, or decoding
